title: Maryland's 4th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Maryland's 4th Congressional District covers most of Prince George's County and a small portion of Montgomery County, suburbs of Washington, D.C. Incumbent Democrat Glenn Ivey, first elected in 2022, faces multiple primary challengers in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, while perennial Republican candidate George E. McDermott is unopposed for the GOP nomination. The district is heavily Democratic (Cook Political Report rates it Solid D), making the Democratic primary the decisive contest. Ivey, a former Prince George's County State's Attorney, is being challenged by healthcare advocate Joseph Gomes, reproductive rights organizer Jakeya Johnson, and others from the left.
polling_note: No opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The district is rated Solid D by major nonpartisan forecasters, and no general-election polling has been conducted publicly.

candidates.name: Glenn F. Ivey
candidates.summary: Glenn Ivey is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Maryland's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024. He previously served as Prince George's County State's Attorney for eight years and as a federal prosecutor. Ivey focuses on public safety, economic opportunity, and infrastructure investments, and is the heavy favorite in the Democratic primary.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, which limits confidence. However, the district fundamentals are well-established: Maryland's 4th is rated Solid D by Cook Political Report, a heavily Democratic district covering most of Prince George's County and part of Montgomery County. Incumbent Democrat Glenn Ivey, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024, is described as the heavy favorite in the June 23 Democratic primary against multiple challengers (Joseph Gomes, Jakeya Johnson, Shavonne N. Hedgepeth, Jonathan D. White). On the Republican side, perennial candidate George E. McDermott—who lost to Ivey by a wide margin in 2024—is unopposed for the GOP nomination with no significant fundraising reported. Given the district's strong Democratic lean (Democratic candidates typically win general elections by wide margins here), Ivey's incumbency advantage, and the absence of a credible general-election challenger, Democrats hold an overwhelming advantage. The lack of polling prevents a high-confidence rating, but fundamentals point to a safe Democratic hold.
